interface.title: FFFBPINN Architecture vs Existing Architecture Demo
interface.field: Scientific machine learning / computational fluid dynamics (physics-informed neural networks for a 1D PDE with a shock, Burgers-type)
interface.stage_of_work: Results analysis and model comparison after training (all runs are precomputed)
interface.what_it_is_for: A dashboard for comparing precomputed PINN, FFPINN, FBPINN and FFFBPINN solutions at several training budgets against a reference PDE solution, using solution and error heatmaps, time-slice cross-sections, log-scale error bar charts and a baseline-relative statistics table.

data.note: The presets (1K, 2.5K, 5K and 10K epochs × 4 architectures, 16 combinations) and the reference solution load when the page opens, with '5K Epochs: PINN' pre-checked. No upload or file input exists. The sidebar starts collapsed and has to be opened with the Toggle Sidebar arrow (screens/001.webp → screens/005.webp). Reloading the page clears all selections.

features.name: Multi-select run picker driving a linked comparison dashboard
features.general: Tick any number of items from a grid of model × setting combinations. Every view (field maps, profiles, bar charts, table) redraws with one panel, curve or row per ticked item, in the order you ticked them.
features.specific: Check any of 16 'NK Epochs: ARCH' boxes in the sidebar. The Solution/Error heatmaps, 1D cross-sections, L2/L∞ bars and Comparative Analytics table all update. Unchecking everything leaves every view blank.
steps: open the sidebar
check one or more epoch/architecture combinations
uncheck ones you no longer need
switch tabs to see the same selection in each view
serves_tasks: Choose a set of runs to compare side by side
Compare the same method across training budgets
Repeat the error-map comparison for one method across training budgets

features.name: Reference-vs-prediction field grid with per-model absolute-error maps
features.general: Show a reference 2D field next to each model's predicted field on a shared colour scale. A second view shows each model's absolute-error field so you can find where it fails. Hover reads off values and box-zoom works on one panel. The error maps have no shared colour scale: each panel has its own colour bar, drawn on top of the others, so you have to hover to read values.
features.specific: Solution Heatmaps puts the 'Reference' contour beside one contour per selection over (x,t) with one shared colour bar. Error Heatmaps shows '<run> Absolute Error' contours (inferno), each with its own overlapping colour bar, with hover for x/t/z and box-zoom on the shock.
steps: select runs
open Solution Heatmaps to compare the fields with the reference
open Error Heatmaps
hover a hotspot to read its coordinates and error
drag a box to zoom one panel; double-click to reset
serves_tasks: Compare predicted fields with the reference field
Find where in the domain each model deviates most

features.name: Time-slice cross-section viewer with legend isolation
features.general: Pick one time (slider, typed value, arrow keys, or reset) and see 1D profiles of the reference and every model, plus their pointwise absolute error, at that instant. Out-of-range values give an error message. Legend clicks hide or isolate curves, and the error axis rescales to what is left.
features.specific: Time Slice (t) slider/number box (0–1, step 0.01, ↺ reset to 0.5) drives 'Solution Slice at t=…' and 'Absolute Error Slice at t=…'. Typing 1.5 shows 'Value 1.5 is greater than maximum value 1.' Legend click hides a trace; double-click isolates one.
steps: open 1D Cross-Sections
set t by dragging the slider, typing a value, or pressing arrow keys
click legend entries to hide dominant curves, or double-click one to isolate it
box-zoom on the sharp front
press ↺ to return to t=0.5
serves_tasks: Plot profiles and pointwise error of all selected models at a chosen time
Move to another time and compare again
Hide or isolate curves to read small errors
Zoom into the sharp feature in the profile

features.name: Log-scale error-norm bar charts
features.general: Side-by-side bar charts of two global error norms (relative L2 and relative L∞) for each selected model, on log axes, with hover readout of exact values.
features.specific: Error Metrics tab: 'Rel. L2 Error' (blue) and 'Rel. L∞ Error' (red) bars per combination; hovering a bar shows e.g. (10K Epochs: FFFBPINN, 0.01320739).
steps: select runs
open Error Metrics
compare bar heights on the log scale
hover a bar for its exact value
serves_tasks: Compare global error norms across methods on a log scale
Compare the same method across training budgets

features.name: Baseline-relative accuracy/runtime table with tick-order baseline choice
features.general: A table listing each selected run's error norms and runtime, plus percent error improvement and percent slower/faster against a baseline row. The baseline is chosen from the selection by a fixed rule that depends on the order runs were ticked, which may not be the run the table's title names.
features.specific: Statistics tab, 'Comparative Analytics (Baseline: 10k PINN if selected)': columns Combination, Rel L2, Rel L∞, Runtime, % Improv. (from Rel L2) and % Slower. Despite the title, the baseline is the first-ticked 10K run whose name contains 'PINN' but not 'FFPINN' (10K PINN, FBPINN or FFFBPINN); only if none is selected does the first selected run become baseline. A 10K FBPINN or FFFBPINN ticked before 10K PINN silently becomes Base, so tick 10K PINN first for the intended comparison. Rows whose Rel L2 equals the baseline's show 'Base'.
steps: tick 10K PINN first if you want it as the baseline
select the other runs to compare
open Statistics and check which row shows 'Base'
read % improvement and % slower/faster per row
serves_tasks: Quantify improvement and runtime cost against a baseline run
See how the comparison changes when the standard baseline is absent
